items.title: Ellis Marsalis — Smithsonian Jazz Oral History
items.q: By this time, Lyndon Johnson had changed all the laws around... 1964, Lyndon Johnson, instrumental in passing the civil rights bill.

ctx.x: You already have a family at this point. Branford was already born.

Yeah, we had four kids, and we came back here. By this time, Lyndon Johnson had changed all the laws around. So when I started working at the Playboy Club again, it wasn’t segregated. I stayed there – I don’t know – maybe a year, two years. I forgot. By 1967, I got a call from a clarinet player in Al Hirt’s band, asking me if I’d join it. So I joined Al Hirt’s band from ’67 to ’70.
Had you played in a traditional context before? Did you . . . ?
